title: Converting Between Representations
explanation: LESSON OBJECTIVE
Convert nonlinear functions among equations, tables, graphs and real-world descriptions, preserving exact ordered pairs, features and domain.
CORE IDEA
The same function can be represented in different ways. Every representation must give the same output for each allowed input.
KEY DEFINITIONS

An equation is a symbolic rule; a table contains ordered pairs; a graph plots those pairs; context defines quantities and domain; a vertex is a quadratic turning point; a growth factor is an exponential multiplier.
CORE RULE

With equally spaced inputs, constant first differences indicate linear behavior, constant second differences indicate quadratic behavior, and constant nonzero ratios indicate exponential behavior. Check every candidate equation against known pairs.
HOW IT WORKS
Identify the function family, extract key features (vertex, roots, initial value, ratio), write the equation or table, verify with an independent point, and preserve units and domain.
WORKED EXAMPLE 1 — EQUATION TO TABLE
For y=x²−4 at x=−2,−1,0,1,2 the outputs are 0,−3,−4,−3,0. The vertex is (0,−4).
WORKED EXAMPLE 2 — TABLE TO EXPONENTIAL
At x=0,1,2,3 the outputs 3,6,12,24 double. Initial value 3 and growth factor 2 give y=3·2^x.
WORKED EXAMPLE 3 — GRAPH TO EQUATION
A parabola has vertex (2,−1) and passes through (3,2). y=a(x−2)²−1 and 2=a−1 imply a=3, so y=3(x−2)²−1.
WORKED EXAMPLE 4 — CONTEXT TO FUNCTION
A population begins at 500 and grows 8% annually. P(t)=500(1.08)^t for t≥0; P(0)=500.
DESMOS STRATEGY

Enter y=3(x−2)^2−1 and point (3,2). Look for vertex (2,−1) and the point on the curve. Use it to verify equivalent representations. Why it works: they share ordered pairs. Faster or not? Algebraic substitution is faster for exact coefficients; Desmos checks visually.
COMMON MISTAKES
Use ratios only for equal input steps. A 20% decrease uses factor 0.80, not 0.20. Preserve domain t≥0. Sketches may be approximate, so use exact labeled coordinates.
EXAM STRATEGY
Look for vertex, roots, initial value or growth factor first. Convert using that feature, then verify an additional point to eliminate wrong options.
QUICK CHECK
y=(x−1)²+2 has vertex (1,2). Outputs 4,12,36 have ratio 3. A 20% decrease uses factor 0.80.
LESSON RECAP
Equivalent representations preserve ordered pairs, vertices, roots, initial values and domain. Identify the family, translate and verify.
NEXT STEP
